body_text: Your Instagram followers aren't yours. Here's how to fix that with Klaviyo Social. Generated by Klaviyo AI Written by Jack Squire, Growth & Partnerships Lead at Get Better, this post argues that Instagram followers stay a Meta-owned asset until brands convert that engagement into owned profiles inside Klaviyo. It covers how tools like Instagram tap-to-text and Klaviyo Social's auto-replies turn follows, comments, and DMs into subscribers, and how that connected data then sharpens customer service, UGC programs, and paid ad targeting. Turn engagement into owned subscribers: Instagram tap-to-text and Klaviyo Social's auto-replies across email, text, and WhatsApp let a comment, tag, or DM become an opt-in captured in the moment, rather than routing someone to a separate sign-up form. Follower count becomes actionable data: Once an Instagram account is connected to a Klaviyo profile, follower count can trigger different customer service handling for high-follower customers, plus separate branches or alerts in UGC/ambassador flows offering extra incentives or direct outreach. Instagram data sharpens ad spend and content reach: Social engagement combined with purchase and email data lets brands build lookalike and retargeting segments for Meta, TikTok, Google, and Pinterest, while the Social Content Library syncs tagged Instagram posts and reels (back-populating up to 200) into Klaviyo for reuse across email, SMS, RCS, and WhatsApp. Sign up Get a demo You don't own your Instagram followers. Meta does. Every like, comment, and DM lives on a platform you don't control, disconnected from everything else you know about that person as a customer. At Get Better , our team specializes in CRM strategy and Klaviyo-powered growth. Recently, we've been closing the gap between Instagram and our clients’ owned channels by pulling Instagram data into Klaviyo and putting it to work across customer service , marketing, and retention . Turn followers into subscribers Instagram engagement doesn't have to stay on Instagram. With list growth tools built into Klaviyo, a comment, tag, or DM can become an actual opt-in for the different owned channels within Klaviyo, captured right where the interaction happens instead of routing someone to a separate sign-up form. Instagram tap-to-text is the clearest version of this: someone messages your account and gets a fast path to opt into text message marketing, and from there they become a profile you can communicate with across channels. Klaviyo Social auto-replies work the same way across email, text messaging, and WhatsApp, so the transition from "follower" to "subscriber" happens inside the conversation, not after it. That's the same principle behind the follower count work. Once someone's opted in, you're not just capturing their consent. You're building the profile that makes everything downstream more personal. Give every Instagram follower a number that means something Once someone's Instagram account is connected to their Klaviyo profile, follower count becomes a property you can act on, not just a vanity metric on someone's bio. When customer service, review requests, and everything in between all runs through Klaviyo, you can start to talk to a customer with 200,000+ Instagram followers differently than one with 200. That distinction pays off in two key places: Customer service: When a support ticket comes in from someone with a large following, your team sees it right away and responds accordingly. In practice, that usually means giving them the VIP treatment so they don’t air a bad experience on social media. UGC and ambassador programs: When you're sending review requests or building out user-generated content (UGC) flows, a high follower count is a signal worth acting on. We recommend setting up a branch for anyone with a higher follower count to get extra incentives, or even trigger an alert so someone on your team can reach out directly and ask if they want to be a content collaborator. All both of these moves require is that your follower data lives in the same place where you make your customer service and marketing decisions. Grow smarter with more personal, profitable paid ads The same Instagram data that upgrades your customer service and UGC flows can also make your ad spend work harder. Once social engagement lives in Klaviyo alongside your purchase and email data, you can build segments around your actual highest-value customers and sync them to Meta, TikTok, Google, Pinterest, and more for lookalike targeting . In addition to going after net-new customers who look like your best ones, you can also retarget the people who already know you: browsers, cart abandoners, and engaged followers. Either way, you're spending against signals you actually trust, not just platform-reported engagement. Put your Instagram UGC to work everywhere, not just on Instagram The next opportunity is newer: the Social Content Library that syncs tagged Instagram posts and reels directly into Klaviyo, so you can use that content in email, SMS, RCS, and WhatsApp, not just in your feed. It back-populates up to 200 previously tagged posts and Reels, then keeps syncing new ones on an ongoing basis. That way, timely, relevant content is always surfacing within the account. From there, you can drop that content into whatever channel you're already sending on. Either way, the idea behind it holds up: the UGC your customers create on Instagram is worth more once it can travel to the channels where you're already trying to convert them. title: Why Every Business Should Be Built To Sell (Even If You Never Plan To Sell)
summary: Preparing your business to be sellable isn’t about planning an exit. It’s about building a stronger, more valuable company that gives you options.
body_text: Why Every Business Should Be Built To Sell (Even If You Never Plan To Sell) Share: Copied! Key Summary Although many entrepreneurs believe they have no immediate plans to exit, unexpected life events or market shifts can force a sale at any time, making it essential to remain perpetually prepared. By focusing on key areas—such as documented systems, diversified revenue, and strong leadership—owners inadvertently build a more profitable and efficient company that functions well regardless of whether or not they eventually sell. Cultivating a "sellable" business is ultimately an investment in strategic freedom, as it ensures the company operates as a high-value, resilient asset that provides the owner with more choices and long-term security. Many business owners say the same thing: “I’m not selling anytime soon.” Some never intend to sell at all. They plan to pass the business to family, continue running it indefinitely, or simply can’t imagine walking away from something they’ve spent years building. That may be true today. But life has a way of changing plans. Health challenges, burnout, partnership disputes, family circumstances, economic downturns, or even an unsolicited acquisition offer can alter your timeline overnight. The question isn’t whether you plan to sell. The question is whether your business would be ready if you had to, or if the right opportunity appeared. Preparing your business to be sellable isn’t about planning an exit. It’s about building a stronger, more valuable company that gives you options. Opportunity and Crisis Rarely Give Advance Notice Most business owners expect they’ll have years to prepare for a sale. In reality, many exits happen because circumstances change unexpectedly. A health issue may make it difficult to continue leading the business. A divorce or family transition may require liquidity. A partner may want out. An attractive acquisition offer may arrive years earlier than expected. Or perhaps you’re simply ready for a different chapter after realizing the business depends too heavily on you. When owners are forced into selling before the business is ready, they often lose negotiating power. Buyers recognize operational weaknesses, owner dependency, inconsistent financial reporting and customer concentration. Those risks typically translate into lower offers or fewer interested buyers. Preparation gives you choices instead of pressure. Sellable Businesses Are Better Businesses One of the biggest misconceptions about exit planning is that it’s only useful for owners preparing to retire. The characteristics buyers value are the same characteristics that create healthier businesses. Buyers look for companies with reliable financial reporting, documented systems, recurring revenue, diversified customers, capable management teams and predictable cash flow. These factors reduce uncertainty and make future performance easier to forecast. They also make the business easier to operate. When processes are documented, work becomes more consistent. When customer relationships extend beyond the owner, growth becomes more sustainable. When financial reporting is timely and accurate, decision-making improves. And when leadership responsibilities are shared, owners gain the freedom to step away without the business slowing down. Ironically, preparing a business for sale often creates a company that is more profitable, more efficient and more enjoyable to own. Business Value Is Built Long Before a Sale Many owners assume they can begin preparing once they’ve decided to exit. Unfortunately, business value doesn’t work that way. The improvements that increase enterprise value take time to develop. Buyers want evidence of consistent financial performance, stable operations, recurring revenue and systems that have been working successfully for years, not months. Research from the McKinsey Institute for Economic Mobility found that many otherwise viable businesses close rather than change hands because owners wait too long to prepare for succession or a sale. The report notes that by 2035, roughly six million small businesses will face an ownership transition, yet many owners still postpone planning until their options have narrowed. The best time to build value is long before you think you’ll need it. The Value of Having Options Perhaps the greatest benefit of building a sellable business has nothing to do with selling. A valuable business gives owners flexibility. You can choose to accept an attractive offer or decline it. You can bring in investors to accelerate growth. You can transition day-to-day management to a leadership team. You can take extended time away from the business without worrying that everything will stop. You may even have more options for succession planning or acquisitions. Business value creates strategic freedom. Owners who focus only on generating annual income often overlook the importance of building an asset . Yet for many entrepreneurs, their business represents their largest source of personal wealth. Protecting and growing that asset should be an ongoing priority, regardless of when, or if, you plan to exit. The Bottom Line Building a sellable business isn’t about preparing to leave. It’s about preparing for whatever comes next. No one can predict when circumstances will change or when an unexpected opportunity will arrive. But every owner can choose to build a company that is transferable, resilient and valuable. The same actions that increase a business’s attractiveness to buyers also improve efficiency, strengthen profitability, reduce risk and create more freedom for the owner today. body_text: Tron Inc. Announces Plan to Deepen Integration with TRON Ecosystem and Pursue Super Representative Status by [email protected] | Aug 13, 2026 | Press Releases Winter Park, Florida, Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Tron Inc. (Nasdaq: TRON) (the “Company”), the largest publicly traded holder of TRON (TRX) tokens, today announced a major strategic initiative to deepen its integration in the TRON DAO ecosystem and expand into value-add infrastructure businesses capable of generating recurring on-chain revenue. The Company plans to pursue election as a top-tier Super Representative (“SR”) for the TRON network. SR nodes (27 in total) operate collaboratively to secure the TRON blockchain, produce blocks, validate transactions, and participate in on-chain community governance. In 2025, the TRON network generated total block production rewards of approximately 122 million TRX for the SRs, as well as voting rewards of approximately 1.5 billion TRX distributed to the 27 SRs and the other SR Partners. The Company has accumulated more than 709 million TRX since implementing its Digital Asset Treasury Strategy in June 2025, with its digital asset holdings reflecting a cumulative gain of approximately $15.8 million as of June 30, 2026. By pursuing TRON SR status, the Company intends to participate directly in the success of the TRON network that is uniquely positioned to benefit from the strong demand globally for stablecoin and agentic AI payment solutions. “Seeking election as a TRON Super Representative represents the next phase of our long-term growth strategy,” said Rich Miller, the Company’s Chief Executive Officer. About TRON DAO Founded in 2017, TRON blockchain is one of the world’s most popular layer-1 networks and the dominant settlement protocol for on-chain stablecoin payment. As of July 31, 2026, TRON blockchain hosts about $90 billion in TRC-20 USDT stablecoin, accounting for nearly half of the total global supply. With over 396 million user wallets internationally and cumulative transaction counts approaching 15 billion as of July 31, 2026, TRON blockchain ecosystem is the de facto global standard for on-chain USDT settlement. According to a recent industry report by Allium, an on-chain research institution, about 90% of stablecoin payment volume settles on TRON. Annual USDT transfer volume grew at a rapid pace of over 40% per annum for three consecutive years to nearly $8 trillion in 2025. About Tron Inc. Tron Inc. is a publicly traded company pioneering blockchain-integrated treasury strategies. As the public company with the largest TRON (TRX) tokens holdings, Tron Inc. is committed to transparency, and the adoption of decentralized finance for long-term value creation. In addition, through its wholly owned subsidiary, the Company designs, develops, and manufactures custom merchandise which includes toys and souvenirs for the world’s largest theme parks and other entertainment venues. Many of the Company’s products are based on award winning multi-billion-dollar entertainment franchises that are featured in popular movies and books. The products are distributed worldwide at Walt Disney Parks and Resorts, Universal Parks and Destinations, United Parks and Resorts SeaWorld, Six Flags and other attractions. title: Hilton Brings Canopy Hotels to South East Asia with Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit
summary: Hilton has opened Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit, marking the debut of its lifestyle brand, Canopy Hotels, in South East Asia.
body_text: Listen to this article 0:00 Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit marks Canopy’s first hotel in South East Asia. Less than a 10 minute walk from the Asoke BTS Skytrain and Sukhumvit MRT stations, the hotel offers easy access to Bangkok’s dining, retail, nightlife, and business districts. With public spaces designed by award-winning interior design studio AvroKO, the hotel draws inspiration from Asoke’s dynamic identity through locally inspired interiors, four dining concepts, and curated experiences designed by a dedicated City Curator. The hotel partners with Bangkok-based lifestyle brand LaLaLove on limited-edition merchandise and a dedicated retail showcase, the first in an evolving programme spotlighting Thai makers and artisans who bring the destination’s creative spirit to life. BANGKOK, Thailand – Hilton (NYSE: HLT) has opened Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit , marking the debut of its lifestyle brand, Canopy Hotels , in South East Asia. Set in Bangkok’s vibrant Asoke neighbourhood, the hotel brings together public spaces by award-winning interior design studio AvroKO , four distinctive dining concepts and city-curated experiences that reflect Bangkok’s layered character and creative energy. The opening represents another milestone in Hilton’s expanding lifestyle portfolio across Asia Pacific. Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit - Lobby Located a six-minute walk from the Asoke BTS Skytrain and Sukhumvit MRT stations, the hotel places guests within easy reach of Bangkok’s leading shopping, dining, nightlife, and business districts, including Terminal 21 and Times Square Shopping Centre within walking distance. “Bangkok has long been one of South East Asia’s most compelling cities, and the opening of Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit adds a new dimension to Hilton’s growing lifestyle portfolio in the region,” said Alexandra Murray, area vice president and regional head of South East Asia, Hilton. “With its thoughtful design, distinctive dining and city-curated experiences, the hotel introduces a new way for travellers to experience Bangkok - combining the comfort and ease of feeling at home with the inspiration of being somewhere new, delivered with Hilton’s signature hospitality.” Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit - Staircase Details (L ) & Courtyard (R) The hotel’s design story unfolds across its lobby and restaurants, and draws inspiration from Asoke’s many layers, from its industrial heritage and the glamour of nearby Sri Krung Sound Film Studio, one of Thailand’s early sound-film studios, to the contrast between old and new that defines the city today. These references are translated in a contemporary way across the hotel’s arrival and social spaces, from a bronze façade inspired by vintage film cameras, to a central courtyard that leads guests directly from the street into the heart of the property. Rooms Designed with a Residential Sense of Ease Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit features 174 guest rooms designed as comfortable retreats that allow guests to settle in, recharge and feel at home while experiencing Bangkok. The room mix spans King and Twin Canopy Rooms , Accessible Rooms , Urban View Rooms , Courtyard Rooms , Courtyard Deluxe Rooms , King Canopy Corner Rooms , and three suites: one King Suk Jai Suite and two King Asoke Suites . Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit - Canopy Urban Room (L) & King Corner Room (R) Reflecting Canopy’s high-end boutique approach, the rooms draw inspiration from the warmth and familiarity of Thai family homes once found along Sukhumvit Soi 12, reinterpreted through a contemporary lens. Curved forms, softened edges and warm neutral materials create a calm, residential feel, while industrial-inspired finishes nod to the nearby Klong Toey port district and Asoke’s evolving urban character. A signature blue Paa Khram (ผ้าคราม) fabric canopy above the bed pays tribute to one of Thailand’s oldest handwoven textiles, becoming a defining feature of the room design. Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit - Top: Interconnecting Room (L) & Canopy Room Twin (R), Bottom: Asoke Suite For guests travelling together, the hotel offers flexible room configurations, including nine pairs of interconnecting rooms that create a more private, suite-style arrangement through a shared entrance area, and seven pairs of connecting rooms with a door between rooms for easy access while maintaining separate spaces. These options are ideal for families, friends and small groups travelling together. Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit - Rooftop Pool Beyond the rooms, guests can spend time at the rooftop pool, where the hotel’s skyline setting offers a quieter perspective on one of Bangkok’s most energetic districts. The hotel also features a 24-hour fitness centre for guests who want to keep to their routine while travelling. Dining from Day to Night Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit - Top: Studio 1930 (L) & Cante (R), Bottom: SoolHaus Fire-led cooking, seasonal Thai ingredients, and bold flavors take center stage across Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit's four restaurants and bars. Cante , the hotel’s signature Spanish fire grill and taberna, brings together wood-fired dishes and sharing plates inspired by Barcelona, Valencia and Andalusia, with design cues from Southern Spain’s layered cultural heritage that echo the richness and diversity of Asoke. SoolHaus offers a Korean-inspired cocktail bar that will cater to Bangkok’s vibrant and diverse late-night drinking scene, while Luso is an all-day café championing Bangkok-roasted coffees and premium Thai-sourced teas from independent artisan producers. Completing the lineup, rooftop pool bar Glint delivers the city’s spectacular skyline alongside cabanas and craft cocktails. Inspired by Bangkok’s Creative Spirit Staying true to Canopy’s belief that every destination has its own character, Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit connects guests to Bangkok through local collaborations and curated experiences that reveal the creativity, culture, and stories that shape the city. The hotel has partnered with Bangkok-based lifestyle brand LalaLove , whose contemporary Thai craftsmanship and creative spirit closely reflect the hotel’s own connection to the city. The collaboration spans across exclusive opening merchandise to a dedicated retail showcase within the hotel, signalling the first in an evolving programme of partnerships with Bangkok's independent makers and artisans. Guests are also invited to explore Bangkok through experiences led by the hotel’s dedicated City Curator , designed to reveal an authentic side of Bangkok. These include the Klong Saen Saeb Boat Experience , which introduces guests to neighborhood cafés, creative spaces and riverside finds along one of the city’s most distinctive waterways; Morning Neighborhood Walks , offering a slower look at Asoke as local eateries, independent cafés and community favorites come to life; and Postcards from Asoke , a creative keepsake experience that invites guests to capture their impressions of the neighborhood and send themselves a personal memento of their time in the city. Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit - Courtyard “Canopy Hotels are designed to help guests feel at home, wherever they are in the world, through thoughtful design, genuine connections, and experiences inspired by each destination,” said Alex Coleman, vice president and global brand leader, Canopy Hotels. “Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit is a strong expression of that vision, drawing from the energy of Asoke and channelling it into every touchpoint, from design and dining to experiences that connect guests to the city beyond the expected. As the brand continues to grow its global footprint, we are proud to welcome Bangkok into a portfolio of hotels that share a genuine commitment to local character.” “Sukhumvit Soi 12 has always held a special place in our story. Through patience, resilience, and the dedication of an extraordinary team, we have transformed what was once an empty site into a destination that honors the spirit of Asoke while creating new opportunities for people to gather, connect, and experience one of Bangkok’s most vibrant neighborhoods. Together with Hilton as our partner, we are confident to debut the first Canopy Hotel in South East Asia. It is the kind of product we are passionate about bringing to market: distinctive, experience-driven, and designed with purpose,” said Ishmit Bajaj, managing director, LLAN Asset. Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit is located at 98, 98/1 Sukhumvit Soi 12, Klongtoey, Klongtoey, Bangkok, 10110. Nightly room rates start at THB 5,700++ (approximately USD 170 ++) for room only, with fully flexible booking options and free changes or cancellations up to 24 hours before arrival. Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit is part of Hilton Honors, the award-winning guest loyalty program for Hilton's 28 world-class brands. Hilton Honors members who book directly through preferred Hilton channels receive access to instant benefits, including a flexible payment slider that allows members to choose nearly any combination of Points and money to book a stay, an exclusive member discount and free standard Wi-Fi. Members also have access to contactless technology exclusively through the industry-leading Hilton Honors mobile app, where Hilton Honors members can check-in, choose their room and access their room using Digital Key. Asoke Unlocked: An Exclusive Opening Offer To celebrate its opening, Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit is launching "Asoke Unlocked" , an exclusive pre-opening offer available to the first 100 guests. Guests booking a minimum two-night stay in a Canopy Courtyard Room or above will receive: 10,000 Hilton Honors Bonus Points THB 500 dining credit to enjoy across the hotel's restaurants and bars An exclusive limited-edition Canopy x LalaLove pouch For reservations and more information, visit canopybangkoksukhumvit.com , call +66 2 146 2888, or email Canopy_bkk_reservations@hilton.com . FAQ: Hilton Brings Canopy Hotels to South East Asia with Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit is a 174-room high-end boutique hotel located on Sukhumvit Soi 12 in Bangkok, marking Canopy’s first hotel in Southeast Asia. The hotel is located on Sukhumvit Soi 12, 600 metres from Asoke BTS Skytrain station – less than a 10 minute walk from the BTS-MRT interchange. The opening marks Canopy’s debut in Southeast Asia and introduces the brand’s “At Home, in the World” philosophy to Bangkok - creating a stay experience that combines the comfort and ease of feeling at home with the inspiration of discovering somewhere new. AvroKO designed selected public spaces at Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit, including the lobby, Luso and Cante. The guest rooms and SoolHaus were designed separately. The hotel draws inspiration from the layered identity of Asoke, including references to the historic Sri Krung Sound Film Studio, the Port of Bangkok and the neighborhood’s evolving urban landscape. The hotel features four dining concepts: Cante, a fire-grilled Spanish restaurant; SoolHaus, a Korean-inspired late-night cocktail bar; Glint, a rooftop pool bar; and Luso, an all-day café serving Bangkok-roasted coffees and premium Thai-sourced teas. Yes. The hotel offers thoughtfully curated experiences led by a dedicated City Curator, designed to help guests connect with Bangkok’s culture, creativity and hidden stories. Experiences include the Klong Saen Saeb Boat Experience, Morning Bangkok Walks and Postcards from Asoke. “Asoke Unlocked” is an opening offer available to the first 100 qualifying bookings. Guests booking a minimum two-night stay in a Canopy Courtyard Room or above will receive 10,000 Hilton Honors Bonus Points, THB 500 dining credit and a limited-edition Canopy x LalaLove pouch. Guests can visit canopybangkoksukhumvit.com , call +66 2 146 2888, or email Canopy_bkk_reservations@hilton.com . Media Contact Geraldine Ling Hilton – Asia Pacific geraldine.ling@hilton.com About Hilton Hilton (NYSE: HLT) is a leading global hospitality company with a portfolio of 28 world-class brands comprising more than 9,400 properties and nearly 1.4 million rooms, in 144 countries and territories. Dedicated to fulfilling its founding vision to fill the earth with the light and warmth of hospitality, Hilton has welcomed over 4 billion guests in its more than 100-year history. Named as the No. 1 World’s Best Workplace by Great Place to Work and Fortune, Hilton aims to create the best culture for its 500,000 team members around the world. Hilton has introduced industry-leading technology enhancements to improve the guest experience, including Digital Key Share, automated complimentary room upgrades and the ability to book confirmed connecting rooms. With the free Hilton Honors app , guests can book their stay, select their room, check in, unlock their door with a Digital Key and check out, all from their smartphone. Visit stories.hilton.com for more information, and connect with Hilton on Facebook , X , LinkedIn , Instagram and YouTube . About Canopy Hotels Canopy Hotels deliver a high-end boutique experience and sense of home during the excitement of travel. Each property's layered, inviting design, considered food and beverage program, and intentionally crafted touchpoints connect guests to the locale while delivering a high level of care in each stay. Located in global destinations spanning continents and cultures, the Canopy portfolio includes nearly 50 open properties across 15 countries and territories, with over 40 under development around the world. Experience Canopy Hotels by booking at canopyhotels.com or through the industry-leading Hilton Honors app . Hilton Honors members who book directly through preferred Hilton channels have access to instant benefits. Learn more about Canopy Hotels at stories.hilton.com/canopybyhilton , and follow the brand on Facebook , Instagram and X . About LLAN Asset LLAN Asset (formerly Lucky Living) is a Thailand-based real estate investment and development company focused on creating distinctive residential, and hospitality destinations. For nearly two decades, the company has built a reputation for introducing differentiated concepts that respond to evolving lifestyles and create enduring value. Guided by a long-term perspective, LLAN Asset creates places with distinct identities that enrich communities and stand the test of time. Learn more at llanasset.co.th

title: Wynn Organizes Jiangxi Study Tour for Macao and Taiwan Youth to Carry Forward the Spirit of the Long March
summary: Tracing Red Revolutionary Heritage and Witnessing the Achievements of Rural Revitalization Macao, Aug 3, 2026 – To commemorate the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March and...
body_text: Tracing Red Revolutionary Heritage and Witnessing the Achievements of Rural Revitalization Macao, Aug 3, 2026 – To commemorate the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March and promote the enduring spirit of the Long March, while fostering a stronger sense of national identity among young people, the Wynn Care Foundation, with the support of the Jiangxi Chinese Overseas Friendship Association, organized the “Commemorating the 90th Anniversary of the Red Army’s Long March Victory — 2026 Macao and Taiwanese Youth Study Tour to Jiangxi” from July 26 to 30, 2026. The delegation visited Nanchang, Jinggangshan, Xiushui, and Pingxiang, where they participated in red culture study programs, youth exchange activities, and rural revitalization visits. Centered on retracing China’s revolutionary heritage and reflecting on the spirit of perseverance, the tour combined exchanges among youth from Jiangxi, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan, intangible cultural heritage experiences, and firsthand exposure to rural revitalization initiatives. Through these activities, participants gained a deeper understanding of China's history, culture, and development achievements, further strengthening their sense of national identity and patriotism. The delegation was led by Ms. Linda Chen, Standing Committee Member of the Jiangxi Provincial Committee of the CPPCC (Macao Region); President of the Wynn Care Foundation; and President, Vice Chairman, and Executive Director of Wynn Macau, Limited. The 28-member delegation comprised representatives from the Youth Committee of the Macau Chamber of Commerce, the Macau Leisure Tourism Services Innovation Association, the Macao Young Entrepreneur Incubation Centre, Wynn’s emerging young leaders, and some youths from Taiwan currently working in Macao. Through immersive visits to revolutionary heritage sites, traditional cultural landmarks, and rural development projects, the program encouraged participants to draw inspiration from the nation’s development journey and strengthen their commitment to contributing to society. The tour also aimed to empower young people to serve as bridges for exchange and cooperation, fostering deeper connections between Macao and the mainland while contributing youthful energy to the country’s continued development. The first stop of the tour was the De’an Yimen Chen Cultural Park, a site dedicated to preserving a nationally recognized intangible cultural heritage. Participants gained insights into traditional Chinese values including loyalty, filial piety, benevolence, righteousness, mutual support, and devotion to the nation. They also attended the opening ceremony of the 11th Jiangxi-Hong Kong-Macao-Taiwan Youth Exchange Program, themed “Remembering the Long March Together, Embracing the Future with Youthful Energy.” During the event, youth representatives from Jiangxi, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan exchanged perspectives on youth development and their responsibilities in the new era. These interactions further deepened participants’ understanding of national affairs, strengthened their appreciation of the country’s development, and fostered greater unity and shared aspirations among young people across the four regions. The delegation then travelled to Xiushui County to attend the Completion and Handover Ceremony of the Soy Products Processing Factory in Zhanfang Village of Xiushui County, together with the Launch Ceremony for the First Direct Shipment of Xigang Tofu to Macao. The ceremony was hosted by Mr. Qiu Xiuhua, Member of the Standing Committee of the Xiushui County Committee and Deputy County Magistrate. Representatives from the Xigang Town Government introduced the project’s development journey, operational scale, and future plans. During the ceremony, Ms. Linda Chen presented a commemorative donation plaque to Mr. Che Li, Deputy County Magistrate of Xiushui County, marking the commencement of the factory’s operations. Following the ceremony, guests toured the production facility to gain a firsthand understanding of its standardized manufacturing processes and sampled a range of specialty soy products. The visit highlighted the tangible achievements of Jiangxi-Macao collaboration in supporting distinctive rural industries and advancing rural revitalization initiatives. The Soy Products Processing Factory in Zhanfang Village of Xiushui County is a flagship rural revitalization initiative supported by the Wynn Care Foundation. The commencement of the factory’s operations marks the successful entry of the region’s intangible cultural heritage product, Xigang Fried Tofu, into the Macao market. The unique product is now available in all Nam Yue Group supermarkets, establishing a stable channel for the direct supply of specialty products from Jiangxi to Macao. The project has not only injected new momentum into rural economic development in Xiushui County, but also leverages Macao’s unique strengths as an important platform for the country’s opening-up. By fostering resource sharing and industrial collaboration between Jiangxi and Macao, the initiative has helped create a new model of cooperation characterized by industrial development, cultural revitalization, improved livelihoods, and mutual prosperity. It serves as a practical example of supporting China’s rural revitalization strategy while contributing to high-quality development. The delegation then travelled to Pingxiang, where members trekked across the alpine meadows of Wugong Mountain and enjoyed the breathtaking beauty of China’s natural landscapes, gaining a deeper appreciation of the country’s rich cultural heritage and enduring civilization. For the final leg of the study tour, the delegation visited Jinggangshan, the cradle of the Chinese Revolution. Participants toured key revolutionary sites including Huangyangjie Outpost, Wulongtan, the Beishan Martyrs Cemetery, the Jinggangshan Revolutionary Museum, and Mao Zedong’s Former Residence in Ciping. Through these visits, they gained a deeper understanding of China’s revolutionary history, paid tribute to the sacrifices of revolutionary martyrs, and reflected on the perseverance and ideals that shaped the Long March. The experience also deepened their appreciation of the enduring significance of the Jinggangshan Spirit and the Long March spirit, and how these values continue to inspire dedication, resilience, and patriotism among younger generations. Participants shared that the study tour had not only deepened their understanding of China’s revolutionary history and traditional culture, but also strengthened their appreciation of the responsibilities entrusted to the younger generation in the new era. They expressed a commitment to transforming what they had learned and experienced into motivation for future growth, carrying forward the spirit of the Long March, sharing China’s stories with confidence, and fostering a stronger sense of national identity and patriotism. Looking ahead, they hope to align their personal aspirations with the country’s development, contribute their talents and energy to the nation’s modernization and rejuvenation, and to do so with resolute passion, responsibility, and commitment.

"Our success is rooted in responsible decision-making and actions," said Joseph Saab, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, International Paper. Some of the ways IP demonstrates its commitment to ethics include: Our Code of Conduct serves as a compass for how we conduct ourselves every day and helps us successfully navigate ethical challenges on the job. Learn more about our Code of Conduct here. Speak UP! policy makes it easy for employees, suppliers and others to talk to someone about a concern, clarify understanding of our policies, or ask a question about ethics in action. Our HelpLine is available to report unethical conduct 24/7. We have a zero retaliation policy against retaliation against anyone who makes a report, raises a concern or cooperates with a HelpLine investigation in good faith. "Congratulations to International Paper for achieving recognition as one of the World's Most Ethical Companies®. Behind this honor is a true dedication and a commitment to advancing business integrity. This approach is good for business – employees and other stakeholders value companies that prioritize the kinds of practices we measure with our process," said Erica Salmon Byrne, Ethisphere's Chief Strategy Officer and Executive Chair. That data undergoes further qualitative analysis by our panel of experts who spend thousands of hours vetting and evaluating each year’s group of applicants. This process serves as an operating framework to capture and codify best-in-class ethics and compliance practices from organizations across industries and from around the world. title: Marti Technologies Launches Ride-Hailing Service in 10 New Cities Across Türkiye
summary: Expands Marti’s Ride-Hailing Service Availability from 20 to 30 Cities, Representing Approximately 85% of Türkiye’s GDP …...
body_text: Marti Technologies Launches Ride-Hailing Service in 10 New Cities Across Türkiye August 12, 2026 6:00am EDT Download as PDF Expands Marti’s Ride-Hailing Service Availability from 20 to 30 Cities, Representing Approximately 85% of Türkiye’s GDP ISTANBUL--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Marti Technologies, Inc. (“Marti” or the “Company”) (NYSE American: MRT), Türkiye’s leading mobility super app, today announced the launch of its ride-hailing service in 10 additional cities across Türkiye , expanding Marti’s ride-hailing footprint to 30 cities and approximately 85% of Türkiye’s GDP . Marti is expanding its ride-hailing service in response to demand, supply, and growth rates in cities outside Türkiye’s largest city, Istanbul, exceeding expectations. The share of Marti’s ride-hailing riders located outside of Istanbul reached 45% as of August 11, 2026 , up from 35% as of August 11, 2025 . Over the same period, the share of Marti’s registered drivers based outside of Istanbul grew from 25% to 36% . “The pace and breadth of our growth outside Istanbul has been particularly encouraging,” said Oguz Alper Oktem, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Marti. “The strong demand and rapid adoption we are driving across our markets are reinforcing our confidence in the opportunity to build Türkiye’s largest and most comprehensive ride-hailing network. With this expansion, Marti now reaches 30 cities across Türkiye, representing approximately 85% of the country’s GDP, and significantly increasing the scale and reach of our platform.” Marti’s newest wave of service launches includes Balıkesir, Çanakkale, Edirne, Erzurum, Hatay, Kahramanmaraş, Sivas, Şanlıurfa, Trabzon, and Van . These markets were selected based on demonstrated ride-hailing demand and limited availability of substitute transportation options . Marti first entered the ride-hailing market in 2022. Following this latest expansion, Marti’s services will now reach approximately 85% of Türkiye’s GDP , up from approximately 80% previously. The expanded footprint represents another significant step toward Marti’s long-term objective of building a nationwide ride-hailing network. Marti reaffirms its previously announced fiscal year 2026 financial guidance of $85 million in revenue and $7 million in Adjusted EBITDA. The Company expects the new city launches to be accretive to its financial performance starting in 2027. About Marti: Founded in 2018, Marti is Türkiye’s leading mobility app, offering a wide variety of transportation services. Marti operates a ride-hailing service that matches riders with car, motorcycle, and taxi drivers; offers delivery services; and operates a large fleet of rental e-mopeds, e-bikes, and e-scooters. title: Perion CEO Tal Jacobson on Building AI That Works Quietly and Performs Loudly
summary: The next phase of AI in marketing may be defined less by the companies with the most visible AI products and more by those that make the technology useful within marketers’ existing workflows.
body_text: You're reading Entrepreneur United Kingdom, an international franchise of Entrepreneur Media. Artificial intelligence has become one of the loudest stories in business. Companies are racing to deploy copilots, launch AI products and announce new models, but for Tal Jacobson, CEO of Perion , the most valuable AI may ultimately be the technology that attracts the least attention. “The best AI is the AI that disappears into the workflow,” Jacobson says. “If marketers have to constantly think about AI, you may be adding another layer of complexity instead of removing it.” Rather than asking marketers and media buyers to adopt another standalone platform, the next generation of advertising technology will increasingly work within the systems and processes they already use. The goal is not to make AI more visible, but to help marketing teams make better decisions and produce stronger business outcomes. From AI Visibility to Business Value The first wave of AI in marketing was largely about visibility. Companies wanted to show they were adopting the technology through chatbots, copilots, generative creative tools and other AI-powered products. As AI becomes embedded throughout the marketing process, the questions are becoming more practical. Is it improving media efficiency? Reducing wasted spend? Helping teams respond faster? Producing measurable incremental outcomes? “Companies aren’t going to be measured by how many AI tools they have,” Jacobson says. “They’re going to be measured by how AI is improving business results.” That philosophy is reflected in the Perion One Platform, which connects planning, creative, media activation, optimization and measurement through an independent operating system. It is designed to help marketers use campaign signals to inform decisions about spend, pacing, creative and performance. “The question isn’t, ‘Where did we use AI?’” Jacobson says. “The question is, ‘Did we make a better decision, and did that decision produce a better outcome?’” The Harder Problem Is Coordination Advertising platforms can already optimize campaigns within their own environments. The harder challenge is coordinating decisions across them and replicating success across them. Modern advertising is fragmented across CTV, digital out-of-home, display, social, retail media, and other channels. Each environment generates its own signals, applies its own optimization logic, and measures performance differently. “Every platform can tell you how it’s performing inside its own walls,” Jacobson says. “The harder problem is understanding what all of those signals mean together, and then deciding what to do next.” Perion’s approach is to connect those signals around an advertiser-defined business objective. Its AI Agent, Outmax, operates within Perion One as an execution layer, helping allocate media spend, manage pacing, and optimize toward outcomes across channels and platforms, including YouTube, Meta, TikTok, CTV, Digital out of Home, Open Web, Audio and more . “When every signal can make the next decision smarter, optimization stops being a series of disconnected actions and becomes a continuous process,” Jacobson says. The broader opportunity is to make AI the connective tissue across the marketing stack. It does not need to replace every platform. It can help teams interpret signals, coordinate decisions and respond more quickly across environments that have traditionally operated in silos. Year One Unified the Infrastructure. Year Two Show Adoption. Building an AI-first technology company is one challenge. Transforming an established public company around a new operating model is another. For Jacobson, Perion’s first phase was about bringing its capabilities together under a unified infrastructure. The next is about proving the value of that transformation through adoption, customer results, and financial performance. “The first year was about bringing the pieces together,” Jacobson says. “Now the job is to prove that this infrastructure creates measurable value at scale with the adoption of our AI technologies with our customers.” The leadership challenge is balancing transformation with continuity. Marketers should not have to abandon established workflows because the technology behind the scenes is changing. They should experience better coordination, faster decisions and clearer connections between media activity and business outcomes. “Transformation is not successful because you reorganized the company,” Jacobson says. “It’s successful when customers feel the difference and the business results show it.” Perion’s strategy is to maintain clear customer-facing solutions while making the underlying infrastructure more unified and intelligent. Within Perion One, you’ll find the conversational interface, Ask Perion, which is designed to help marketers plan complex campaigns, interpret campaign performance, explore scenarios, and understand what is driving results and how to translate those insights into action. Performance Should Be Loud The next phase of AI in marketing may be defined less by the companies with the most visible AI products and more by those that make the technology useful within marketers’ existing workflows. “AI doesn’t need to be the hero of the story,” Jacobson says. “The customer, the outcome and the performance should be the hero.” That is the idea behind Perion’s transformation. The first year was about unifying the infrastructure. The second is about demonstrating what it can deliver for marketers and the businesses they serve. The best AI works quietly, improves the decisions marketers already make and lets the results speak for themselves. Artificial intelligence has become one of the loudest stories in business. Companies are racing to deploy copilots, launch AI products and announce new models, but for Tal Jacobson, CEO of Perion , the most valuable AI may ultimately be the technology that attracts the least attention. “The best AI is the AI that disappears into the workflow,” Jacobson says. “If marketers have to constantly think about AI, you may be adding another layer of complexity instead of removing it.” Rather than asking marketers and media buyers to adopt another standalone platform, the next generation of advertising technology will increasingly work within the systems and processes they already use. The goal is not to make AI more visible, but to help marketing teams make better decisions and produce stronger business outcomes.

title: Why You're Losing Organic Search to AI (and How Video Fits In)
summary: AI search tools can't watch your videos, but they can read them. Learn how to optimize video metadata so AI can find, understand, and cite your content.
body_text: If your organic traffic or content engagement has been slipping, AI search is a major factor. When someone gets their answer directly from an AI Overview or a chat tool, they often never click through to a website at all. That shift alone is reshaping how much organic traffic reaches any site. 43% of Google searches now show an AI Overview instead of a list of links, so fewer of those searches ever turn into a click to your site, and video is often hit hardest. AI search tools like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews can’t watch a video, so if yours has no transcript, no structured description, and no clear metadata, it’s invisible to the tools now answering your buyers’ questions before they ever reach you. The fix is to give AI the same signals it uses to understand a webpage. Optimizing your video metadata adds those signals, so your video content can start showing up in AI generated search results and LLM recommendations. The shift in search Buyers aren’t just scrolling results anymore, they’re asking AI tools directly and getting an answer handed to them. 71% of B2B software buyers now use AI in their vendor research . And when a vendor gets cited in an AI answer, it carries real weight, 85% of B2B software buyers think more highly of a vendor when AI cites them in a response . For years, marketers asked: can people find my video? Now there’s a second question that matters just as much: can AI understand it? If AI can’t understand your video, it can’t recommend it, cite it, or surface it to a buyer who’s asking the exact question your video answers. Why AI can’t watch your videos Search engines and AI tools are good at reading text. A webpage is built from text, so it’s naturally legible to a crawler. It can read the headline, the body copy, the headers, and figure out what the page is about. Video doesn’t work that way. A video is a media file, not text. Drop one into a webpage and AI has no built-in way to know: What the video actually covers Who it’s meant for What format it is (demo, webinar, customer story) What questions it answers Why it’s relevant to the person asking None of that is a flaw in your video. It’s just a gap in how the content gets described to a machine. Google’s guidance on VideoObject schema and Microsoft’s guidance for Bing and Copilot both point to the same fix: video hosted with structured data . Without it, even a great video sits invisible next to text content that AI can read easily. Hosting videos on YouTube vs. your site Structured data solves what AI can read, but where that video lives still matters. You can put your video on YouTube, and for pure reach, you probably should. But there’s a catch most teams miss. When you embed a YouTube video on your site, search engines and AI index the version hosted at youtube.com, not the one on your page. If that video gets cited or ranked, the click doesn’t come to you. It goes to a YouTube watch page, surrounded by recommended videos, half of them your competitors. Hosting your video on your own domain keeps the indexable version, and the traffic that follows it, on your site. When AI or search surfaces that video, the buyer lands in your funnel. There’s one more thing YouTube can’t do, tell you who watched. Vidyard ties video engagement to real contacts in your CRM, so a view becomes pipeline intelligence your sales team can act on, not just a number in an analytics tab. How AI understands your videos There are two different experiences happening around every video you publish. What people experience: the visuals, the narration, the story, the content itself. That’s the layer built for humans, and it’s where most production time goes. What AI and search experience: the title, the description, the transcript, the tags, and the structured metadata sitting around that video. For a lot of teams, that layer is an afterthought. Both layers are answering the same core question: what is this video actually about? People get that answer by watching. AI gets that answer from the text signals around the video. Clearer signals help AI understand and surface your content. What optimizing metadata does is give your video an opportunity to be understood. A video AI can’t read is a video AI can’t recommend. What marketers are really trying to solve Strip away the jargon and most marketing teams are chasing the same handful of outcomes. Help people discover our videos. You’ve published dozens or hundreds of videos across webinars, demos, and customer stories. Most of them are sitting there with no plan for anyone new to find them. Improve visibility in AI search. Your team has spent years on SEO. Now there’s a whole new surface, AI answer engines, and most video content hasn’t been set up for it at all. Capture more non-brand demand. Someone asks ChatGPT a question your product solves, and your competitor’s content gets cited instead of yours. That’s demand you’re losing before a prospect ever hits your site. Scale without creating more manual work. Nobody has time to write custom metadata for every single video by hand. Whatever the fix is, it has to work at the scale your video library already exists at. AI search discoverability is now a marketing-wide responsibility Search discoverability used to sit almost entirely with the SEO team. Now it touches nearly every role in marketing. Role What video in AI search means for them CMO / VP Marketing Needs visibility into how the brand shows up in AI answers, not just organic rankings Demand Generation Has to think about AI search as a new top-of-funnel channel, alongside paid and organic Product Marketing Needs product and use-case language written in a way AI can pull into an answer Content Marketing Owns making sure every published video has the text signals AI needs to understand it Digital Marketing & SEO Extends existing technical SEO practices to cover structured data for video Marketing Operations Needs a scalable, repeatable process instead of one-off manual fixes for campaigns with video No single role owns this by themselves anymore. The teams that move fastest are the ones who stop waiting for someone else to fix it. 5 ways to optimize video metadata for AI search Write descriptive titles. A title should say plainly what the video covers, not just tease it. AI uses the title as one of its strongest signals for what the video is about. Write meaningful descriptions. A short, generic caption doesn’t help. A clear description that explains the topic, the audience, and the format gives AI something real to work with. Publish full transcripts. A transcript turns your video into readable text. It’s the single biggest thing you can do to make a video legible to AI. Use consistent tags. Consistent tagging across your video library helps AI (and your own team) understand how videos relate to each other and to specific topics. Expose structured metadata. Structured data, like VideoObject schema, tells AI exactly what type of content it’s looking at in a format built for machines to read. Doing all five by hand, across an entire video library, isn’t realistic for most teams. Platforms like Vidyard automate this, so your videos get these signals without adding manual work to your team’s plate. The next chapter of video marketing We spent years optimizing content for people, then for search engines. Now it’s AI’s turn to understand what we’ve made. Your videos already do the hard work of explaining your product and telling your customers’ stories. The only thing missing is a way for AI to read that work. Optimizing your video metadata with Vidyard takes minutes, not a new workflow. Vidyard can automatically expose each video’s title, description, transcript, and tags as structured data AI and search engines can read. You can apply settings across an entire folder or customize individual videos, and it works with all the ways you embed and share video without changing how you already publish. That way your videos can still live on your own site, so you keep the traffic instead of sending viewers to a third-party platform. Want to make your video content easier for LLMs to discover with Vidyard’s metadata optimization? See it in action . Frequently asked questions How do I get traction on ChatGPT, Google and other AI search engines? Give your videos clear, complete text signals: descriptive titles, real descriptions, full transcripts, and structured metadata. That’s what both traditional search and AI answer engines rely on to understand and surface content. Can AI answer engines cite my videos? Yes, AI answer engines can cite video content when they can read and understand it. The more clearly a video’s metadata explains what it covers, the more likely it is to be surfaced in a relevant answer. What information is included when I optimize my video metadata? Optimizing metadata typically includes the video title, description, transcript, tags, and structured data like VideoObject schema, the same signals covered in the five ways above. Should I host my videos on YouTube or on my own site? You can host on YouTube, and for reach, it’s worth doing. Just know that search engines and AI cite the version hosted on youtube.com, not the one on your page, so that traffic goes to YouTube instead of your site. Hosting on your own domain keeps the click, the funnel, and the viewer data yours to act on. Does optimizing video metadata work with every video? It works best on videos with real spoken or written content to draw a transcript and description from, such as webinars, demos, and customer stories. How do I know which videos to optimize? Start with your highest-traffic or highest-intent videos, like product demos and customer stories, then expand to the rest of your library over time. Does optimizing video metadata guarantee rankings or AI citations? Optimizing metadata gives AI the information it needs to understand your video, but no platform can guarantee a ranking or a citation in an AI answer.

title: Why Water Beads Can Be Dangerous: Hidden Risks Every Parent Should Know

body_text: Water beads have become increasingly popular in recent years. They are used for children's sensory activities, floral decorations, plant hydration, and even home décor. Their bright colors, soft texture, and ability to grow dramatically in water make them fascinating to both children and adults. However, safety experts and healthcare professionals continue to warn that these tiny products may present serious hazards inside the home. What appears to be a harmless toy or decorative accessory can become a medical emergency if swallowed or placed in the nose or ears. This article explains the potential dangers of water beads, why experts recommend caution, and how families can reduce the risks while choosing safer alternatives. What Are Water Beads? Water beads are small polymer spheres designed to absorb water and expand many times their original size. They are commonly used for: Sensory play activities Flower arrangements Home decorations Plant watering Educational science projects Once placed in water, these tiny beads can expand dramatically, making them visually appealing and enjoyable to handle. Unfortunately, this same expanding property is what makes them potentially dangerous. Why Are Water Beads Considered Dangerous? The primary concern is accidental ingestion. Young children naturally explore objects by placing them in their mouths. Since water beads often resemble colorful candy, jelly sweets, or small fruit, children may mistake them for food. If swallowed, the beads can continue absorbing liquid inside the digestive system and increase significantly in size. This expansion may block the intestines, interfere with normal digestion, and require emergency medical treatment. Medical experts have reported that delayed diagnosis is another challenge because water beads may not always be easily detected using standard imaging techniques. Potential Health Risks Accidental exposure to water beads may lead to several serious complications, including: Intestinal blockage Choking hazards Vomiting Severe abdominal pain Constipation Dehydration Damage to the digestive tract Emergency surgery in severe cases The danger is not limited to swallowing. Children have also been known to place water beads inside their noses or ears, where the beads may continue expanding after absorbing moisture. This can lead to pain, infection, hearing problems, or tissue damage if not treated quickly. Symptoms That Should Never Be Ignored Parents and caregivers should seek immediate medical attention if a child has access to water beads and develops symptoms such as: Repeated vomiting Persistent stomach pain Swollen abdomen Refusing food or drinks Constipation Difficulty swallowing Unusual drowsiness Signs of dehydration Even if symptoms seem mild initially, professional medical evaluation is recommended because complications may develop over time. Why Pets Are Also at Risk Water beads are not only dangerous for children. Dogs, cats, and other household pets may mistake them for treats or toys. Once swallowed, the beads can expand inside the digestive tract and potentially create life threatening intestinal blockages. Pet owners should keep these products completely out of reach or avoid bringing them into homes with curious animals. Decorative Uses May Still Present Risks Many adults use water beads in decorative bowls or flower arrangements. Although this may seem safer than children's play, loose beads can easily fall onto the floor without being noticed. Curious toddlers or pets may later discover and swallow them. Standing water around decorative beads may also encourage bacterial growth if containers are not cleaned regularly. Safer Alternatives to Water Beads Fortunately, there are many safer options available. For sensory activities, consider: Colored rice Kinetic sand Homemade play dough Silicone sensory toys Large textured blocks For home decoration, alternatives include: Glass marbles Decorative stones Wooden beads Artificial fillers Dried flowers Pebbles These options provide visual appeal without the same expansion risk. Water Bead Safety Tips If water beads are already in your home, follow these important precautions: Store them in locked cabinets. Never leave expanded beads unattended. Keep them away from babies and toddlers. Supervise older children closely during use. Clean spilled beads immediately. Dispose of unused beads safely. Keep pets away from storage containers. Read manufacturer safety instructions before use. Families with children under five years old may wish to avoid water beads altogether. Frequently Asked Questions Are water beads toxic? Most concerns relate to their physical expansion after swallowing rather than toxicity alone. However, always follow manufacturer guidance and seek medical advice if accidental exposure occurs. Can adults safely use water beads? Adults may use them for decorative purposes, but households with young children or pets should carefully consider the potential risks. What should I do if my child swallows a water bead? Seek immediate medical attention, even if your child appears well. Early assessment can help prevent serious complications. Should schools and childcare centers use water beads? Many safety experts recommend evaluating safer alternatives for sensory activities, particularly where young children are involved. Final Thoughts Water beads may appear harmless, but experts continue to raise concerns about the dangers they present to young children and pets. Their ability to expand dramatically after absorbing water makes accidental ingestion particularly dangerous. Parents, caregivers, teachers, and pet owners should understand these risks and consider safer alternatives whenever possible. Awareness and prevention remain the best ways to avoid potentially serious accidents. Source: Mail, product safety guidance, and expert commentary referenced in the original report. Readers should also consult official health authorities and product safety organizations for the latest recommendations. Disclaimer: This article is intended for educational and informational purposes only. It should not be considered medical, legal, or professional advice. If you suspect a child or pet has swallowed a water bead or is experiencing symptoms after exposure, seek immediate medical or veterinary assistance.

title: Why Judicial Orders Alone Cannot Stop Election Black Money in India
summary: Explore why judicial orders cannot stop election black money in India. Analyze statutory loopholes, RPA 1951, Section 77 limits, and party funding.
body_text: Why Judicial Orders Alone Cannot Stop Election Black Money in India Aug, 2026 • 12 min read Judicial directives enforce election rules, but statutory amendments by Parliament remain vital to close funding loopholes. Context Judicial orders alone cannot eliminate black money from Indian elections. Supreme Court rulings address procedural enforcement mechanisms . However, statutory carve-outs in the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and Income Tax Act, 1961 permit unrestricted political party expenditure and non-transparent cash donations. Recent judicial directives from the Supreme Court of India have tightened seizure reporting timelines , struck down anonymous funding tools, and restricted prosecution withdrawals. Yet statutory loopholes still separate candidate spending caps from unlimited party budgets. Until Parliament acts, judicial oversight remains a temporary palliative rather than a structural cure. Why Election Funding Reform Is Back in the Spotlight The Supreme Court of India recently tightened procedures for handling seized assets during elections to curb illicit financial flows. In State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026 INSC 868) , the Supreme Court issued strict procedural directions to prevent political interference during polls as reported in August 2026. The Court's key directions establish tight operational boundaries: 24-hour reporting window : Authorities seizing cash or assets linked to electoral offences must report to a District Magistrate or competent court within 24 hours with written reasons establishing a prima facie nexus . Time-bound trials : The bench imposed a mandatory one-year deadline to complete investigations into electoral offences and asked High Courts to set up special courts. Restriction on withdrawals : State governments cannot unilaterally withdraw criminal prosecutions against candidates during elections without prior High Court approval . While these directives strengthen investigative integrity under Article 324 , the Court emphasised that its residuary authority operates only where statutory law is silent. It cannot override express legislative enactments. Discuss with Superkalam What time limit did the Supreme Court set for investigating electoral offences in State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026)? Ask Now The Supreme Court in State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026) mandated strict 24-hour reporting and a 1-year investigation limit for electoral asset seizures. What the Supreme Court Has Tried to Fix The Supreme Court of India has consistently deployed constitutional remedies to enforce transparency in political party operations. Judicial interventions seek to protect the voter's fundamental right to information under Article 19(1)(a) . Key rulings demonstrate this constitutional approach: Accountability and Audits : In Common Cause v. Union of India (1996) , the Court held that Election Commission powers under Article 324 include auditing party accounts and demanding financial disclosures. Striking Anonymous Funding : In Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India (2024 INSC 113) , the Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme, 2018 as unconstitutional. The Court ruled that anonymous political contributions violated the voter's right to know donor identities. Despite these landmark verdicts, judicial orders face sharp institutional limitations . Courts cannot rewrite statutory codes or establish new spending caps from the bench. Discuss with Superkalam How does Explanation 1 of Section 77 create a gap between candidate and party spending limits? Ask Now The Legal Loophole That Keeps Black Money Alive The Representation of the People Act, 1951 creates a stark contrast between candidate expenditure limits and party spending. Under Rule 90 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, statutory ceilings cap individual candidate spending at ₹95 lakh for Lok Sabha constituencies in larger states and ₹75 lakh in smaller states. Yet political party expenditure remains entirely uncapped by statute . This gap originates in Section 77(1) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. While candidates must record all personal election expenses, Explanation 1 excludes party spending on star campaigners and general propaganda from candidate accounts. In Kanwar Lal Gupta v. Amar Nath Chawla (1975) , the Supreme Court ruled that party spending benefiting a specific candidate must count towards that candidate's cap. Parliament later amended Section 77 to nullify this ruling , which the Court upheld in P. Nalla Thampy Terah v. Union of India (1985) . Separately, under Section 123(1) of the RPA, 1951, bribery is a corrupt practice , but invalidating an election requires proving direct consent from the candidate or their agent. What Past Committees Warned Us About Party Finances Government-appointed committees have long warned that unregulated private capital distorts political equality. Key reform proposals highlight distinct strategies to address off-the-books wealth: In-Kind State Funding : The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) recommended partial state funding strictly in-kind —supplying fuel, paper, and broadcast airtime—to recognised national and state parties while excluding independent candidates. Prerequisites and Disclosure Timelines : The 255th Law Commission Report (2015) deemed total state funding unviable under present fiscal conditions. It argued that state aid requires mandatory inner-party democracy , decriminalisation of politics, and strict disclosures. The report recommended inserting Section 29F into the RPA, 1951, forcing parties to submit audited statements within 75 days for assembly polls and 90 days for general elections. Why Financial Reporting and Tax Exemptions Fail The Income Tax Act, 1961 grants political parties broad exemptions that complicate tracking untaxed wealth. Two primary statutory mechanics govern these tax benefits: Section 13A Tax Exemptions : Registered parties receive 100% tax exemption on house property, capital gains, and voluntary contributions. Parties maintain this tax-free status by submitting audited accounts and disclosing voluntary donations over ₹20,000 under Section 29C of the RPA, 1951. Cash Donation Thresholds : The Finance Act, 2017 amended Section 13A to cap cash donations at ₹2,000 per donor. However, enforcement remains weak because parties can aggregate unrecorded micro-donations below the threshold without revealing donor identities. Ask Now How to Fix Electoral Funding: The Way Forward Eradicating election black money requires holistic legislative action rather than relying on ad-hoc judicial directions. Parliament can reform electoral finance through targeted statutory amendments: Revising Candidate Expense Rules : Re-evaluate Explanation 1 of Section 77 of the RPA, 1951 to count party spending on behalf of candidates against candidate expenditure caps , restoring the principle in Kanwar Lal Gupta (1975) . Enforcing Audit Timelines : Insert Section 29F into the RPA, 1951 as proposed by the 255th Law Commission Report to give strict ECI disclosure deadlines binding statutory power. Tightening Tax Exemptions : Condition Section 13A tax exemptions under the Income Tax Act, 1961 on full digital auditability and lower contribution reporting thresholds. Introducing State Support : Adopt in-kind state funding under the Indrajit Gupta Committee model to reduce cash reliance while preserving a level playing field for recognised parties. Key Takeaways The Election Commission of India requires comprehensive legislative backing to effectively regulate political party finances and eliminate electoral black money. Judicial Boundaries : Supreme Court rulings, including 2026 INSC 868 , strengthen investigative timelines under Article 324 but cannot override explicit legislative statutes or statutory carve-outs. Expenditure Asymmetry : Section 77 of the RPA, 1951 caps candidate spending at ₹95 lakh/₹75 lakh while leaving political party election expenditure completely uncapped under Explanation 1. Tax Exemptions : Section 13A of the Income Tax Act, 1961 offers 100% tax exemptions to parties, while cash donation limits of ₹2,000 under the Finance Act, 2017 are easily circumvented through fragmented cash reporting. State Funding Principles : The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) advocated partial in-kind state funding for recognised parties, while the 255th Law Commission Report deemed absolute state funding unviable without inner-party democracy and mandatory disclosures. Statutory Reform Needed : Effective regulation requires inserting proposed Section 29F into the RPA, 1951 to enforce mandatory 75-day and 90-day expenditure disclosure timelines.
